event: Thursday of week five: you wake in room 8, in Lin's narrow bed, grey light on the drawings.
Lin is awake already, sitting up with her sketchbook on her knees, drawing you asleep.
"Don't move," she says. "Nearly." You lie still and watch her; she finishes, and shows you.
It's you with your hair across your face and one hand open on her pillow. Under it: Thursday.

memory.fact: The morning after, Lin drew Nala asleep in her bed, and wrote Thursday under it.

event: She kisses you good morning, shy again in daylight, and laughs at herself for being shy.
You go up to 15 in yesterday's clothes; Bea is sitting on her bed lacing her running shoes.
She looks up at you, searching your face. "Well?" she says. "Is she all right?"
"She's all right," you say. "She's lovely." Bea's whole face goes soft. "Good," she says. "Good."

memory.fact: Told Lin was all right, lovely, Bea's whole face went soft: Good. Good.
Told Lin was all right, lovely, Bea's whole face went soft: Good. Good.

event: Then she grins. "You've got charcoal on your neck." She licks her thumb and rubs it off.
"Two days," Bea says, standing up, bouncing on her toes. "Two days. I'm going to be sick."
You run the shore with her; she runs too fast, and you let her, and she slows down after a mile.
Breakfast: Lin comes down late, pink, with her hair down; she sits beside you and eats everything.

memory.fact: Lin came down to breakfast pink, her long hair loose in daylight for once, and ate everything.

event: Priya looks from Lin to you and back, and opens her mouth; Bea kicks her under the table.
Morning: History of Magic in the lecture hall; the lecturer writes 1816 on the board.
The Glass Winter, she says: the year with no summer, when spells across the north came out thin.

event: Glims guttered; kettles took an hour; menders cracked the cups they were mending. A mystery.

memory.fact: In the Glass Winter glims guttered, kettle charms crawled, and menders cracked the cups they mended.

event: Kit writes fast. Lin draws a cracked cup in the margin of your notes, very small.
Amara asks if they ever found out why. The lecturer smiles. "Next week," she says. "Patience."
After, Kit walks with you to the Practice Hall. "Thin spells," she says. "Imagine it."
"Tomorrow," Kit says. "Six. The cinema. I've booked it." She looks at you. "Still on?" Still on.

memory.fact: Kit has booked the cinema for Friday at six; asked if it's still on, Nala said: Still on.

event: Shiv sits with you. "Saturday," she says. "I've written something rude in Irish on a bedsheet."

memory.fact: For Bea's race Shiv has written something rude in Irish on a bedsheet.

event: Bea, overhearing, chokes on her soup. "Shiv. You can't." Shiv grins. "Watch me, bow."

event: Two: practical; calling again, further now: the whole length of the bench, six feet.
You call the thimble the full six feet; it comes slow and steady, and you catch it clean.
Your head aches by the third time; Foundations, you think: the body keeps the account. You stop.

memory.fact: Nala called a thimble the full six feet, twice; the third time her head ached, and she stopped.

event: Bea calls her spoon six feet and it arrives gently in her palm; she stares at it, then cheers.

memory.fact: Bea's spoon came the full six feet to her palm, gently; she stared at it, then cheered.

event: Lin calls a pen down the bench like a leaf on a stream; the demonstrator watches, and nods.
Afternoon: you finish your focus essay in the Snug, by the iron grate, with tea Kit brought up.
You write about Kit's ring, and the drawing Lin made of you, and a tin medal a small boy wears.
At the end you write: it should remember, if what it remembers is someone being loved.

memory.fact: Nala's focus essay ends: It should remember, if what it remembers is someone being loved.

event: Kit reads it upside down across the sofa, and squeezes your foot in place of speaking.

memory.fact: Nala's focus essay ends: It should remember, if what it remembers is someone being loved.

The morning after, Lin drew Nala asleep in her bed, and wrote Thursday under it.

event: Seven: life drawing in the Drawing Room. The model tonight is Morwenna, the rowing captain.
She sits nude on the dais as calm as on the jetty, arms folded, amused.
Lin draws her fast, six times in an hour; you draw her twice, and the second time it's good.
"Look more," Lin murmurs. "Draw less." Your third drawing has Morwenna's grin in it, nearly.
Morwenna dresses after and comes to look at the drawings. She stops at yours, and laughs.

pictured.coverAfter: And sits down nude on the stool, as calm as on the jetty.

event: "That's me telling Lindqvist to sit up," she says. "Spot on. Tell Bea to sleep tonight."

memory.fact: Morwenna sat nude for life drawing; at Nala's drawing of her grin she laughed: Spot on.

event: Half past nine: you fill the flask; Yusra's on tonight, ten till six, the way she is Thursdays.
She comes down at quarter to ten; she sees you at the foot of the stairs and her face eases.
"Every time," she says, before you can. You hand her the flask. She holds your fingers on it.
Yusra says, low: "You were in room 8 last night. Lin's room. I'm the warden. I hear doors."

memory.fact: Lin came down to breakfast pink, her long hair loose in daylight for once, and ate everything.

event: You go still. Yusra's mouth twitches. "Good," she says. "She's been lonely, that one. Like me."

memory.fact: Yusra guessed Nala spent the night with Lin, and said Good: she's been lonely, that one. Like me.

event: "Saturday," she says. "After the race. Front door." She touches your cheek once, and goes.
In 15 Bea is lying on her back on the rug, staring at the ceiling, her hands on her stomach.
"I'm visualising," she says. "Morwenna says visualise. I'm visualising being sick in the boat."
You lie down on the rug beside her. You give her Morwenna's message: sleep tonight.

memory.fact: Two nights before the race Morwenna sent Bea word by Nala: sleep tonight. Nala gave it.
Two nights before the race Morwenna sent Bea word by Nala: sleep tonight. Nala gave it.

event: Bea groans. Then she laughs. Then she takes your hand on the rug. "Will you be at the jetty?"
"At the wall," you say. "Shouting." Bea turns her head and looks at you. "Where I kissed you."
You get into bed; she lies awake a long while, rowing in the dark with small movements of her hands.
You hold her till the movements stop, and her breathing slows, and she's asleep.

memory.fact: Two nights before the race Bea rowed in the dark with her hands till she slept, Nala holding her.
